body:
## Summary

Implement the ID broker / serve-proxy wire protocol decided on #5792 (decision record: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5792#issuecomment-6719076837), as a mode of the id binary. Parent design: #5671 (its fallback ordering, trust model, and E2E boundary are unchanged and bind this work). Downstream consumer: #5798 (fleet surface for the broker role), which configures this role once it exists.

## What to build (per the #5792 decision record)

- Leg establishment: TLS 1.3 over TCP 443, through HTTP CONNECT where the egress requires a proxy; optional WebSocket binary-message adapter carrying the same frames where CONNECT is denied.
- Frame codec: 4-byte big-endian length prefix plus typed frames (OPEN, DATA, CLOSE, WINDOW_UPDATE, PING, PONG, RESUME, RESUME_ACK, ERROR); DATA payload capped at 16 KiB.
- Multiplexing: per-leg stream IDs (odd/even by initiator), broker-side stream-ID mapping between client and server legs, per-stream credit flow control (initial 64 KiB per stream, 1 MiB per connection), priority scheduling in three classes (control, interactive, bulk), and the two-connection class split (control+interactive on one connection, bulk on another).
- Keepalive: PING after 25 s idle (plus/minus 20 percent jitter), leg declared dead after 3 unanswered PINGs, broker closes legs silent for 120 s into the resume window.
- Resumption: broker-issued session token bound to the endpoint identity key, RESUME signed by that key, per-stream sequence numbers with delivered-up-to vectors, replay of exactly the unacknowledged tail, 5-minute resume window, in-memory broker state only.
- Authorization and logging per the decision invariants: authenticated broker use by default, no payload logging, metadata-only operational logs.

## Invariants (from the decision record)

The broker never holds or derives content keys and never terminates the E2E layer; control frames never queue behind DATA; credit is never exceeded (overrun closes the leg with ERROR); the broker persists nothing to disk in v1; resumption never duplicates or reorders per-stream delivery.

## Tests

Name an oracle per the repo testing doctrine: frame codec round-trip and cap enforcement via property-based tests (oracle: decode-encode identity plus the 16 KiB cap invariant); resumption via model-based tests against a simple per-stream ordered-delivery model (oracle: the model); keepalive/dead-leg timing against a fake clock. CI runs the suites per repo policy.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Frame codec, mux, flow control, keepalive, and resumption implemented in the id binary serve-proxy mode, matching the #5792 record section by section.
- [ ] Tests above pass in CI, including the no-duplicate / no-reorder resumption property.
- [ ] A broker forwards E2E ciphertext between a UDP-denied client leg and a server rendezvous leg in an end-to-end test, with the broker demonstrably unable to read payload plaintext.
- [ ] Any deviation from the #5792 decision is recorded on #5792 explicitly, not silently forked.

## Relations

Design: #5792 (decision record). Parent: #5671. Downstream: #5798. Programme: epic #2056.
Filed by queue worker task 12789 (lane code-y), 2026-11-08.
